To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL-4 inhibits the adhesion of Natural Killer (NK)-cells on vascular EC by interfering with the LFA-1/ICAM and VLA-1/VCAM adhesion pathway.
IL-4 inhibits the binding and cytotoxic activity of NK cells on vascular EC.
IL-4 inhibits the binding and cytotoxic activity of NK cells on EC, and this is mediated by the downregulation of CD18-dependent adhesion pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of IL-4 in regulating the interaction between NK cells and endothelial cells.
the role of NK cells in vascular inflammation.
the influence of IL4 on the interaction of NK cells with vascular endothelium, which may be relevant to the pathogenesis of inflammatory and autoimmune diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL-4 inhibits the adhesion and cytotoxicity mediated by NK cells through the beta2-integrin adhesion pathway.
IL-4 inhibits the interaction of NK cells with vascular EC by interfering with the CD18-dependent adhesion pathway.
IL-4 inhibits the interaction of NK cells with EC, and this is likely to contribute to development of a TH2-type response in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL-4 is a powerful inhibitor of NK cell adhesion and cytotoxicity to vascular EC, and that this effect involves the CD18-dependent adhesion pathway.

IL-4 is a powerful inhibitor of NK cell-endothelial cell adhesion, and that it is a potent inhibitor of the cytotoxicity exerted by NK cells on EC, and this effect is mediated via the down-regulation of the CD18/ICAM pathway.
IL-4 inhibits adhesion of NK cell to EC and that IL-4 does so by inhibiting the beta 2 integrin (CD18) dependent adhesion pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-4 inhibits the adhesion of IL-2 and IL-4 activated NK cells to vascular and endothelial cell, and the cytotoxicity against endothelial cells.
IL-4 inhibits the binding of NK cells to EC and the cytotoxicity against EC.
IL-4 inhibits the adhesion of resting and activated NK cells to endothelium.
